text:
maya: ran a short k/v-store hit-curve sweep across regions + H100/A100 kernels, posting top-level summary and dashboards here: https://dash.internal/redwood/kvcache/sweeps/1842001111 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: TL;DR: hit-rate vs p99 shows clear knee at ~65% hit for long-tail sequences (>1024). H100 fused-kernel wins p50 but A100 with matmul-batched wins sustained throughput at high batch sizes in eu-west.

maya: command we used:
```bash
./bench_run --model gpt-xxl --region eu-west,us-west --gpu h100,a100 --seq-mix "0-64:0.6,65-512:0.3,513-2048:0.1" --kv-prefetch 2 --evict-window 5 --batch-sizes 1,4,8,16 --out s3://redwood-kvbench/1842001111/
```

julian: nice. can you attach the raw csv for p99 per-seqlen bucket? want to plot hit % vs p99 not just overall curves :eyes:

maya: uploaded raw CSVs: s3://redwood-kvbench/1842001111/h100_eu-west.csv and .../a100_us-west.csv. also put a condensed table in the dash.

hao: curious — what kernel variants were used on H100? did you test fused-attn-v2 + cutlass-mma vs the older triton kernels?

maya: H100 ran fused-attn-v2 + cutlass-mma (default), A100 ran triton-matmul-batched fallback for the matmul path. I added a small run with h100+triton; results in extras folder.

ops-bot: benchmark-runner: job 1842001111 finished. artifacts: https://ci.internal.redwood/artifacts/1842001111 (logs + perf traces)

ira: quick read: looks like page-in latency dominates p99 for seqlen>1024 when hit-rate < 70%. smaller seqlens (<128) show almost linear relationship between hit% and token latency.

sam: pulled numbers: h100 eu-west, seq>1024, batch=8 -> hit 62% => p50 11ms, p95 38ms, p99 92ms. a100 us-west, same mix -> hit 59% => p99 110ms (higher tail).

julian: interesting that H100 tail is lower even with more page ins — maybe cutlass kernels overlap transfers better? any traces showing async DMA overlap?

maya: yes — perf trace shows better overlap on h100 cutlass path. I added per-request timeline on the dash (hover to see transfer vs compute).

hao: thought: try raising kv-prefetch to 4 for long sequences to see if extra prefetch reduces p99 more than it increases memory pressure. could be a win in eu region where latency matters more.

maya: queued a targeted run (prefetch=4, evict-window=8) for eu-west h100 batch 8 at 1842001200. will post results.

katie: if prefetch=4 reduces p99 significantly we should consider a region-based default profile: eu-latency -> prefetch=4, us-cost -> prefetch=2. open a tiny RFC? :thumbsup:

sam: quick note on eviction policy: current LRU window 5 seems sensitive to long multi-turn chat. if we bump eviction-window to 8 we hold more KV pages and hit-rate rises ~4-6% in our sims, but memory footprint jumps ~12%. tradeoff depends on reserved capacity sizing.

ira: for Dedicated customers we can offer an "interactive" profile with larger eviction-window + prefetch aggressive — document cost impact with the dashboard.

maya: results from queued run: prefetch=4, evict-window=8, h100 eu-west, batch=8 -> hit 69%, p99 58ms (was 92ms). So big tail win. memory increase as expected. uploaded diff artifacts to s3://redwood-kvbench/1842001111/prefetch4/

julian: wow that's a solid regression for latency. does quality/outputs change? any divergence due to prefetch ordering or racey KV reads?

maya: no model output differences observed in sampling runs. KV reads are deterministic, prefetch only affects timing.

katie: can someone file a small ops playbook and PR to default profiles (console + docs) with a note about cost delta? i'll pair with eng-runtime to spec rollout.

maya: assigning follow-ups: julian — viz of hit% vs p99 per-seqlen bucket (csv -> dashboard). hao — run h100/triton combo for comparison. katie + ops — draft profile + cost note. i'll paste links and small writeup in a GH issue.

julian: ack, will do.

hao: will run combos and post by EOD.

maya: thanks all :rocket:
